![](/images/uq1.jpg){width="100%"}

LADAL tools are self-contained interactive tools that run entirely in your browser — no installation of R or any other software is required. Click a launch button on any tool card below, wait for the environment to load (typically 1–3 minutes on first launch), and start working with your own texts.

LADAL offers two types of tools, each suited to different access situations:

- **Shiny Tools** — polished point-and-click applications. Require an Australian or New Zealand university login (AAF or Tuakiri). Launch via the ARDC BinderHub.
- **Jupyter Notebook Tools** — flexible interactive notebooks. Available to **everyone worldwide** via MyBinder and GESIS — no login required.

---

## Shiny Tools {#shiny-tools}

```{=html}
<div class="section-intro">
  <strong>What are Shiny tools?</strong> These are fully graphical, point-and-click applications built with R Shiny. You upload your texts, configure the analysis using menus and sliders, and download the results — no coding required at any step.<br><br>
  <strong>&#x1F512; Access:</strong> All Shiny tools launch via the <strong>ARDC BinderHub</strong>, hosted by the <a href="https://ardc.edu.au" style="color:#51247A;font-weight:600;">Australian Research Data Commons</a> on the NeCTAR Research Cloud. A university login via <strong>AAF</strong> (Australian Access Federation) or <strong>Tuakiri</strong> (New Zealand) is required. If you are outside Australia or New Zealand and need access, please <a href="mailto:m.schweinberger@uq.edu.au" style="color:#51247A;font-weight:600;">contact Martin</a> to discuss alternatives — the Jupyter Notebook tools below are available to everyone worldwide.
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="server-notice">
  <b>&#x26A0; One server at a time:</b> Each tool runs on its own server session, and you can only have <b>one server running at a time</b>. Before switching to a different tool, please stop your current server first:
  <ol>
    <li>Go to <a href="https://binderhub.rc.nectar.org.au/hub/home">binderhub.rc.nectar.org.au/hub/home</a></li>
    <li>Click <b>Control Panel</b> in the top navigation bar</li>
    <li>Click the red <b>Stop My Server</b> button</li>
    <li>Wait a few seconds until the button disappears, then launch your next tool</li>
  </ol>
</div>
```

### Text Preparation Tools {#shiny-preparation}


### Text Analysis Tools {#shiny-analysis}

```{=html}
<p class="tool-group-desc">These tools perform linguistic and statistical analysis on your texts — from concordancing and collocation to sentiment, topic modelling, and network visualisation.</p>

    </div>

      <p>Search for words or phrases across uploaded texts and generate KWIC (Keyword-in-Context) displays. Results can be sorted by left or right context and downloaded as Excel or CSV.</p>
      <a href="/tutorials/concordancing_tutorial/concordancing_tutorial.html" class="tool-learn-link">&#x2192; Concordancing Tutorial</a>
```

## Jupyter Notebook Tools {#jupyter-tools}

```{=html}
<div class="section-intro">
  <strong>What are Jupyter Notebook tools?</strong> These are interactive R notebooks that run in a JupyterLab environment in your browser. They are slightly more code-visible than the Shiny tools but still require no local installation, and they are available to <strong>everyone worldwide</strong> — no university login needed.<br><br>
  <strong>&#x1F310; Two open-access platforms — no login required:</strong>
  <ul style="margin:8px 0 0 0; padding-left:1.2em; line-height:1.7;">
    <li><strong>MyBinder</strong> — a community-run open platform. Free for everyone. Startup typically takes 2–3 minutes.</li>
    <li><strong>GESIS BinderHub</strong> — hosted by the GESIS Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences in Germany. Free for everyone and often faster than MyBinder. A good first choice if MyBinder is slow.</li>
  </ul>
  Both platforms are equivalent in functionality. If one is unresponsive, simply try the other.
</div>
```

### Text Preparation Notebooks {#jupyter-preparation}

```{=html}
<p class="tool-group-desc">Notebook-based tools for cleaning and annotating text data before analysis.</p>
<div class="tool-cards-grid">

  <!-- Concordance Explorer -->
  <div class="tool-card">
    <div class="tool-card-header jn">
      <div class="tool-icon">&#x1F50D;</div>
      <div class="tool-card-header-text">
        <h3>Concordance Explorer</h3>
        <p>KWIC concordances — find any word or phrase in context</p>
      </div>
    </div>
```
